security_model.description: HyperQL's security model uses DEFINE ACCESS ROLE and CREATE USER. Fine-grained filtering is provided by DEFINE ACCESS POLICY.

definitions.syntax: DEFINE ACCESS ROLE RoleName [ GRANT NAMESPACE NamespaceName PERMISSIONS [Permission, ...] [CASCADE | NO CASCADE], DENY NAMESPACE NamespaceName PERMISSIONS [Permission, ...] [CASCADE | NO CASCADE], GRANT NODE TypeName PERMISSIONS [Permission, ...], DENY NODE TypeName PERMISSIONS [Permission, ...], GRANT EDGE TypeName PERMISSIONS [Permission, ...], DENY EDGE TypeName PERMISSIONS [Permission, ...], GRANT FIELD FieldName PERMISSIONS [Permission, ...], DENY FIELD FieldName PERMISSIONS [Permission, ...] ];
definitions.description: Grants or denies permissions over namespaces, types, and fields. DENY takes precedence over GRANT. v0.19 adds CASCADE/NO CASCADE support for namespaces.

definitions.syntax: CREATE USER username WITH PASSWORD "credential_or_provider_ref" [ROLES [Role1, Role2]];
ALTER USER username [ SET PASSWORD "new_credential", ADD ROLES [RoleName, ...], REMOVE ROLES [RoleName, ...] ];
GRANT ACCESS ROLE RoleName TO username;
REVOKE ACCESS ROLE RoleName FROM username;
DEFINE ACCESS POLICY PolicyName ON NodeType | EdgeType FOR ACCESS ROLE RoleName USING (condition_expression);
definitions.description: Fine-grained node/edge-level filtering. Transparent to queries. Condition has access to $current_user variable.
definitions.example: DEFINE ACCESS POLICY OwnOrdersOnly ON Order FOR ACCESS ROLE CustomerRole USING (owner_id == $current_user.id);

permission_inheritance.description: Rules governing how permissions propagate through the namespace hierarchy.

rules.name: Downward Cascade
rules.description: A grant on namespace N implicitly grants the same permissions on all descendant namespaces of N to arbitrary depth, unless overridden by a DENY at a descendant level.

rules.name: No Upward Cascade
rules.description: A grant on namespace N confers no permissions on any ancestor or sibling namespace of N.

rules.name: DENY Hard Ceiling
rules.description: A DENY on namespace N overrides any grant at N or any descendant of N, regardless of where the grant was declared. A child-level GRANT cannot override a parent-level DENY.

rules.name: Additive Child Grants
rules.description: A grant may be issued at a child namespace without a grant at the parent. This grants access only to the specified namespace and its descendants, with no effect on the parent or siblings.

rules.name: CASCADE Default
rules.description: Grants cascade downward by default. NO CASCADE restricts a grant to the specified namespace only, with no propagation to descendants.

permission_resolution_rules.description: Rules governing interaction between namespace permissions, type-partitioned storage, and composable polymorphism via EXTENDS.

rules.name: Partition Authority (Instance Data)
rules.description: Read and write permissions for node and edge instance data are governed by the namespace of the type's storage partition. Field SchemaId ownership does not determine instance data access permissions. Node<T> traversal crosses partition boundaries.

rules.name: Type Reference Authority (Schema Access)
rules.description: Referencing a type by name in a query requires read permission on the namespace where that type is defined. This is a schema-level permission check, separate from instance data permissions.

rules.name: Polymorphic Subtype Visibility
rules.description: A polymorphic MATCH on a parent type includes concrete subtypes only from namespaces the querying user has read permission on. Subtypes in inaccessible namespaces are silently excluded from the result set.

rules.name: Role Traversal Boundary
rules.description: When a query traverses a role or a Node<T> field to a target node, the target node's accessibility is governed by the permission of its storage partition's namespace. Nodes in inaccessible partitions are silently excluded from traversal results.

rules.name: Schema vs. Permission Dependency
rules.description: IMPORT and EXTENDS establish schema dependencies tracked via SchemaIds. They do not create runtime permission dependencies. A namespace that imports another does not automatically inherit permissions over the imported namespace's instance data or types.

rules.name: Write Partition Authority
rules.description: Write permission for creating or modifying a node or edge instance is governed by the namespace of the type's storage partition, regardless of where inherited field SchemaIds are defined.

strict_permissions_mode.description: Switches default silent-filter behavior to loud failure for Rules PERM-8 and PERM-9. Any query that would produce a silently filtered result instead raises [9010] Permission Denied and aborts.
strict_permissions_mode.note: STRICT_PERMISSIONS is distinct from the removed per-file STRICT_MODE. STRICT_PERMISSIONS governs permission boundary behavior only. It has no effect on schema validation rules.
syntax: ALTER NAMESPACE NamespaceName SET STRICT_PERMISSIONS ON;

normative_rules.description: Under STRICT_PERMISSIONS, a polymorphic MATCH that would encounter a subtype in an inaccessible namespace raises [9010] rather than silently excluding the subtype.
Under STRICT_PERMISSIONS, a role traversal or a Node<T> field traversal that would encounter a node in an inaccessible partition raises [9010] rather than silently excluding the node.
STRICT_PERMISSIONS does not affect DEFINE ACCESS POLICY row-level filtering. Access policies always filter silently.

introspection: SHOW EFFECTIVE PERMISSIONS FOR username ON NAMESPACE NamespaceName;

SHOW_EFFECTIVE_PERMISSIONS.description: Returns the fully resolved permission set for a user against a specific namespace, after all grants, denies, and cascades have been applied.

structure.subnamespaces: [{ namespace: String, permissions: [Permission], denied: [Permission] }] /* recursive breakdown

SHOW_NAMESPACE.description: Returns basic metadata for a namespace.

aggregation_functions.description: Aggregation functions operate on collections in RETURN clauses with GROUP BY, @computed properties, and role collections. v0.19: AggFn is a formally separate enum. AggFn calls are a distinct AST variant (AggCallExpr) [Decision 5].
aggregation_functions.structural_rules: AggCallExpr is structurally forbidden in positions that accept only scalar expressions. Valid in: RETURN, WITH (projection), and HAVING.

functions.name: COUNT
functions.desc: COUNT(*) counts all rows; COUNT(expr) counts non-nulls.

role_collection_aggregation.description: Aggregation over (MANY) role collections and List<Node<T>> collections is built-in and does NOT require graph traversal.
examples: MATCH (c:Commute) RETURN c, COUNT(c.passengers) /* passengers is List<Node<Person>> */

sql_style.syntax: RETURN agg_func(expr), group_expr GROUP BY group_expr

with_style.syntax: WITH group_expr AS alias, COLLECT(var) AS collection RETURN ...

user_defined_aggregates.description: Custom aggregations defined via DEFINE AGGREGATE FUNCTION can be used interchangeably with built-in aggregation functions. Must be marked @pure. Graph access is forbidden.
user_defined_aggregates.syntax: RETURN Name(expr1, expr2) GROUP BY group_expr
user_defined_aggregates.example: RETURN p.Department, WeightedAvg(p.Salary, p.PerformanceScore) GROUP BY p.Department;

window_functions.description: Window functions perform calculations across a set of rows related to the current row. v0.19: WindowFn is a formally separate enum. WindowCallExpr carries a WindowSpec [Decision 5].
window_functions.structural_rules: Forbidden outside of RETURN and WITH (projection) contexts.

frame_specification.description: Defines the frame for aggregate and navigation window functions. Valid only when ORDER BY is present.

frame_types.ROWS: Defined in terms of physical row offsets.
frame_types.RANGE: Defined in terms of logical distance. Requires numeric/date ORDER BY.

defaults.with_order_by: RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
defaults.without_order_by: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING

examples: SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY cat ORDER BY date RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
